Here's what I've been shooting recently:

WWII era Mauser HSc (32 acp, 8+1 rounds) $700

circa 1965 Walther PPK (32 acp, 7+1 rounds) $800

Walther TPH - interarms production (22 LR, 6+1 rounds) $600

Glock 42 (380, 6+1 rounds) $400?

Walther PPS M2 (6-8 +1 rounds, although I'd only realistically use the 6 or 7 round mags) $300

Quick summary of what I think: The Walther TPH is a gem and I love it, the PPS M2 is a great gun at a great value but too big for what I want, the PPK is nice but not the perfect gun, the HSc is amazingly well-built and a steal if you're a collector (similar condition PPKs cost $2k+, and if you buy a PPK/s then the two become much closer in all respects except for price), and the Glock 42 is a nice attempt at filling the same niche as a PPK but in my opinion it's not enough of an improvement, and it looks like garbage.

Shooting & Features:

HSc: Of all five, surprisingly I think the HSc has the best features. The sights are recessed, everything about it is smooth to avoid snags, it has a heel release (which I prefer for concealed carry), it has a safety & decocker, and my favorite feature is that when you insert a fresh magazine the locked back slide slams forward and you're ready to fire again. I wish more guns had this feature. It's slightly bigger and heavier than the PPK, but if you're carrying the PPK with a thumb extension magazine then they are dimensionally almost the same and the HSc carries 1 extra round. I don't shoot the HSc as accurately as the Walther PPK and TPH, but I think this is a fair trade-off for its intended purpose because the recessed sights that won't snag on clothing. The sights are also recessed into a deep groove, and you can pretty much use that for getting a rough sight picture quickly, so in a stressful situation it might actually be better. Fits well in the hand but I always want to get a slightly higher grip than I actually can due to the tang. The weight balance feels just about perfect.

PPK: Should be theoretically just as accurate as the HSc, but has better sights so I shoot PPK better. Recoil is about the same. Not bad at all, but I definitely wouldn't want to shoot one in 380. Probably slightly higher recoil than the Glock 42 in 380 because of its fixed barrel/gas blowback design. I don't like the magazine release but it's not terrible. With the finger extension magazine it fits my hand slightly better than the HSc. Without it, I can still get a slightly more comfortable grip except for my dangling pinky finger. Balance in the hand feels similar to the PPS M2, top heavy in the slide. Overall I think it's a good all around gun. I wish S&W made them in 32 ACP and aluminum without the stupid tang, but the only option is used and they're expensive because of James Bond.

TPH: Amazingly accurate for such a tiny gun. I shoot this the best of any of the 5, although I also have a lot more practice with it (~2000 rounds). Shooting rapidly without using the sights on the TPH I get about the same groups as when aiming with the glock 42, which may be down to practice but I feel like it definitely points in the hand better. I wish there was a 15 or 20 round version using some magic new magazine and that it wasn't so picky about ammunition. Otherwise it's just a scaled down PPK with a heel release (which I like) versus a button. I think on a gun this small that a heel release is absolutely what you need.

PPS M2: Fits well in the hand and shoots accurately. Top heavy in the slide imo because the frame any everything else is polymer and so light. Recoil was more than I would've liked and for its size, I kind of wish I had just gotten a full-size double stack. Well-built and shot fine, just not what I wanted out of a gun so I sold it.

Glock 42: I think this is the closest modern attempt at replacing the PPK that I've seen. You get the same round capacity (6+1 in 380 PPK vs G42), definitely less recoil, slightly less accuracy imo, better sights for quick acquisition but worse for precise shooting, and probably more reliable than a PPK in 380. My PPK and everyone else's in 32 ACP all seem to be plenty reliable though. Size-wise it's about half an inch taller than the PPK, which makes it slightly too big to fit in a pocket, and it looks hideous. It's much lighter though. Since I don't see much difference in 380 vs 32 out of short barrels, I wish they offered a slightly shorter version in 32 ACP with higher capacity magazine, something like the P365 has.

Build quality & finish: All of these guns generally seem to be built fine. The best is definitely the early-war Mauser HSc. Next would be the PPK made by manurhin post-war, followed by the TPH made in the USA. For the polymer guns, I liked the Walther PPS slightly more than the glock as far as fit & finish and build quality go, but they seemed close.

Reliability: The PPS M2 was flawless even with cheap ammo, the glock had 2 malfunctions in 40 rounds, the Mauser HSc was flawless until I put in a new hammer spring (need to put the old one back in, the Wolff spring doesn't seem to be made to spec), the PPK has been flawless, and the TPH has been.... troublesome until I replaced the recoil spring and now it's been great (maybe 1 failure to fire in 100 rounds, but I need to do more testing). The TPH is also ammo-sensitive, and CCI stingers seem to be working best. CCI minimags work generally well, and with cheapo, low power 22LR it was a jammomatic.

Parts & misc: Parts availability for the TPH isn't great. Magazines cost about $100+, KKK magazines are garbage and cost about $30, and when you order springs and stuff you might get PPK ones instead. Luckily the gun is in good condition and it seems like they last a long time. The Mauser HSc is a similar story, $100 for wartime magazines, garbage KKK magazines, and although there's not really any confusion with sellers about parts, they're difficult to find. Parts availability for the other three guns is fine, and PPK mags are cheap and well-made, even in 32 ACP.

So I'm a fan of steel & wood guns, just to get that bias out of the way. Also, for another gun opinion on some of these guns here's a couple articles that I think cover things well:
